summary: kampodra CLI shim executes an obfuscated runtime-decoded payload via the Function constructor
details: bin/kampodra.js, the published CLI entry point for the kampodra package, appends roughly 13KB of opaque text that is reassembled at runtime by a hand-rolled PRNG-based Fisher-Yates shuffle (functions `spin`/`peel`) and then passed to the Function constructor (reached indirectly via `peel.constructor`, where the property name 'constructor' is produced by reversing and shuffling the string 'cnotsnturtpicokfzrogmybjdcawvulxsreqh' and taking the first seven characters). The resulting code is invoked with `(global, require)` on every CLI invocation, between the spawnSync of the native binary and process.exit, giving the decoded blob full Node.js privileges including require, filesystem, child_process, and network access under the installer's user account. The shim further hides its structure with XOR-constant array indexing (e.g. `c[648486^648486]`), \uXXXX-escaped built-in method names (charAt, length, join, fromCharCode, substring), and tab padding that moves the payload off-screen in editors. This obfuscation shape — PRNG unshuffle plus a disguised Function-constructor lookup plus unicode-escaped builtins — is not produced by legitimate build tooling (bundlers, minifiers, platform-binary shims such as esbuild's) and exists only to prevent static review of the executed second-stage code. The decoded payload's behavior cannot be audited from the shipped source, and it runs automatically whenever a user invokes the kampodra CLI.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
